source: Hu and Tang (2026) The Winner's Curse in LLM Self-Improvement Loops
finding: Keep-if-better loops where Qwen models rewrite their own instructions: after the first rewrite most proposals are harmful, and the best candidate of a generation is inflated by a predictable amount.
numbers: Oracle runs: 55 to 152 candidates per setting, each scored on 600 held-out items. On TREC 75-100% of first-generation rewrites improved on the seed; later only 4-39% improved on the incumbent; mean held-out effects -0.2 to -13.5 points; candidate-error correlation 0.44-0.60.
limits: Small Qwen models (1.5B-14B, Qwen3.5-4B); tasks TREC, Banking77, GSM8K. Preprint, one author group.
agent_relevance: Direct answer to gap 1. Best-of-N by a self-scored metric overstates gain, and later-stage candidates are mostly worse than the incumbent. Treat the top-scored candidate as inflated.

source: Hu and Tang (2026) The Winner's Curse in LLM Self-Improvement Loops (pre-registered study)
finding: Pre-registered confirmatory study with fresh 600-item gold set and new seeds: greedy loops report selection-set scores far above held-out accuracy when the selection set is small.
numbers: Final selection-set score exceeded held-out accuracy by 13 to 20 points at n=16 selection items and by 1 to 5 points at n=256. Paired reduction about 15 points (14.7-15.9) in three settings, Holm p<=0.04; 10.5 points on Banking77 (p=0.058). Four settings x nine arms x 8 seeds. At n=16 greedy loops ended 0.6 +-0.7 below the seed (4 of 8 seeds lost) while their selection scores rose 12.5 points.
limits: Held-out gain rose with n on TREC (13.7 to 24.2 for 1.5B, 14.0 to 20.4 for 7B) but not on GSM8K; one exploratory finding (Banking77 effect) did not replicate. Small models.
agent_relevance: The selected-vs-fresh gap shrinks with selection-set size roughly from 15 points to 3. A schema needs a separate audit set. Also a live example that exploratory loop findings failed to replicate in the authors' own pre-registered run.

source: Hu and Tang (2026) The Winner's Curse in LLM Self-Improvement Loops (acceptance rules and audit set)
finding: Tested acceptance rules (McNemar, pilot-calibrated Bayes gate, select-then-confirm) did not beat greedy over whole runs; they mainly commit less often. A small never-used audit set removes the average bias of the reported gain.
numbers: At n=16 greedy commits in 44% of decisions, pilot gate 8%, tuned McNemar 6%; 58%, 59%, 46% of those commits are harmful. Gate ended 2.1 +-1.1 points below greedy (p=0.06). Audit on 64 fresh items costs 128 evaluations (a tenth of 1,280) and cuts RMSE of the reported gain from 15.5 to 5.7 points; single estimates still off by about 6 points. Resolving gains of a few points needs a few hundred items.
limits: Gate priors came from pilot runs of the same model and task. Held-out gains with the rules were not better whole-run.
agent_relevance: Gap 2 partly: a frozen pilot-calibrated rule did not lower whole-run harm. Cheap fix that works: score start and current prompt on about 64 unseen items. Report the held-out gain with its uncertainty.

source: Zhang, Xu, Sun, Zhou, Cao, Aggarwal (2026) Towards Reliable LLM Evaluation: Correcting the Winner's Curse in Adaptive Benchmarking (SIREN)
finding: Winner-based reporting after prompt or program search on reused benchmark items is optimistic. A repeated-split protocol that freezes the shortlist removes the bias.
numbers: MMLU-Pro Math, random search, 44 cells: same-data winner bias +3.06 points (M1/M2), SIREN -0.01 (MAE 0.14). DSPy tuner: +1.43 vs -0.05. At 500K budget random search bias +5.19. Simulation: same-data best-of optimism rises from +1.5 pp at 3 candidates to +4.0 pp at 50, tracking sqrt(2 log H); declares an identical system the winner 48.3% to 94.0% of the time; SIREN bias within 0.4 pp and 0.0% false wins.
limits: Needs a fixed shortlist and smooth selection assumption. Bias magnitudes depend on item count (MMLU-Pro subsets).
agent_relevance: Gap 1 closed with numbers: more candidates tried gives more optimism, about +4 points at 50 identical candidates. Freezing the shortlist then evaluating on held-out splits is the working remedy.

source: Shawn (2026) PACE: Anytime-valid acceptance tests for self-evolving agents
finding: Keep-if-score-rises acts as uncontrolled multiple testing. A sequential betting test that commits only on decisive paired evidence stops false commits.
numbers: Qwen2.5 0.5B-3B on GSM8K, SVAMP, ARC-Challenge. With a hidden real gain, greedy commits 30-42% false and 10-33% harmful edits (5 seeds). With no real gain, greedy makes 13.3 +-20.7 self-edits per run, 72-100% false, and loses 4.9 +-3.0 points on the 0.5B agent; PACE commits under 1 per run and holds baseline, about 18% lower eval cost.
limits: False and harmful labels come from a temperature-0 audit, not ground truth (0/5 audit-labelled false commits). Small models, 5 seeds. Hu and Tang report this degradation did not replicate in their pre-registered runs.
agent_relevance: Gap 2: a pre-set test rule (analogue of a fixed decision rule) cuts churn a lot. Whether it raises held-out accuracy is contested (see d03). Value is hygiene and stability.

source: Xu, Yan, Chen, Kechadi (2026) Phantom Gains: Auditing Self-Improvement Against a Measured Null
finding: Auditing three rounds of LoRA self-training on Qwen3-8B against a frozen control run through the same pipeline: seven measurement failures, each of which reverses a reported finding when the null control is missing.
numbers: A single greedy decode ledger shows capability change on an untrained model (largely inference-batching noise); the expansion statistic gives that frozen model a rate of 0.280. Per-problem exact test with FDR control detects nothing on any held-out replicate. Distillation helps hard problems (p<1e-8 vs self-training).
limits: Training study (LoRA), not a scaffold. One base model.
agent_relevance: A frozen-control arm is the analogue of a replication. Any reported gain per problem needs a null measured by re-running the unchanged system.

source: Bellibatlu, Raff, Zhang (2026) JudgeSense: prompt sensitivity in LLM-as-a-judge
finding: Rewording the judge instruction, with the same meaning, changes verdicts on all four tasks, beyond the judge's own run-to-run noise.
numbers: 880 items, 25 judges from 6 providers. Pooled agreement loss (JSS): coherence -0.181, factuality -0.057, preference -0.045, relevance -0.034. With clustering by vendor only coherence (p=0.0008) and factuality (p=0.0076) clear the 0.02 threshold; unclustered SEs are 1.37-1.63 times too small. Collapsing coherence to binary removes 58.6% of the effect. A judge inside an agent harness looks more stable only because its self-agreement collapses faster.
limits: Four tasks, roster weighted to small and mid models; threshold 0.02 set by authors.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: a judge comparing two prompts is itself prompt-sensitive. Use two judge wordings and several judges from different vendors; do not count sibling models as independent.

source: Feng, Shen, Balashankar, Gerner-Beuerle, Rodrigues (2026) Noisy but Valid: statistical evaluation of LLMs with imperfect judges
finding: A small human-labelled set estimates judge TPR and FPR; a variance-corrected threshold then gives finite-sample Type-I control on a large judge-labelled set. Noisy testing beats direct evaluation only if judge quality exceeds a derived threshold.
numbers: Main experiments: human calibration set n_M=100, judge-labelled set n_J=10,000, alpha=0.25 in the main figure; datasets Jigsaw, Hate Speech, SafeRLHF. Reports an 'oracle gap' between estimated and known judge parameters.
limits: Certifies failure rate below a threshold; not a two-prompt A/B test. Tables on FPR per prompt not extracted.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 partly: judge false positives can be controlled if a small human-checked set calibrates the judge. Quantify judge error before using it to rank scaffolds.

source: Derived power calculation (this agent, from d03 and the standard McNemar sample-size formula)
finding: Paired comparison of two prompts on the same items: only items where the two disagree carry information.
numbers: n about (1.645+0.84)^2 * d / delta^2 for one-sided alpha 0.05 and 80% power. For a 3 point gain: d=10% disagreement gives about 690 items; d=20% gives about 1,370 items. Hu and Tang give 'a few hundred' at their task disagreement rates and a detectable 3.2 points at 80% power in their pooled H4 test (32 seed pairs).
limits: Own arithmetic, not from a paper. Ignores judge noise and seed variance, which raise the need.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 minimum N: plan several hundred to over a thousand paired items for a 3-point gain; 20-item pilots can only see big effects.

source: Wang et al. (2026) Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution for Agents
finding: Automatic harness evolution on Terminal-Bench 2.1 fails to beat simple test-time scaling at matched budget and generalises poorly to held-out tasks. Searching with same-benchmark verification signals breaks train-test separation.
numbers: Abstract only: harness evolution gains 80% over search baseline on ARC-AGI-3 and 11% on EdgeBench games at matched budget, but not on Terminal-Bench.
limits: Abstract only (opened:false); gains are task-type specific.
agent_relevance: Gaps 1 and 9: apparent scaffold gains vanish at equal budget on some task types and hold on others. Always include a matched-compute baseline.

source: Authors not recorded (2026) The Model Proposes, the Code Disposes: pre-registered ablation of a verifier-and-acceptance stage
finding: Pre-registered 20-run ablation of a verifier stage in an offensive-security agent: removing the verifier lowers precision of what is shipped.
numbers: Median shipped precision 0.471 with verifier vs 0.353 without (p=0.0087); suppressed findings median 2 vs 0 (p=0.00003); recall not different (p=0.158, equivalence not shown); full design kept 93.8% of true candidates, missed its 0.90 non-inferiority floor (lower bound 0.875). 2x2 study, 40 runs.
limits: Abstract only; two lab targets; human adjudication pending; incomplete ground truth.
agent_relevance: Gap 8 partly: a verify-before-claim stage that suppresses findings raised precision by about 12 points at some recall risk. The model verifier did the work; deterministic rules alone suppressed nothing.

source: Benjamin et al. (2018) Redefine Statistical Significance (Nature Human Behaviour; preprint PDF)
finding: Re-read to check the thresholds the schema uses. p=0.05 is weak evidence; p=0.005 is substantial.
numbers: Two-sided p=0.05 corresponds to Bayes factors of about 2.5 to 3.4; p=0.005 to about 14 to 26. With prior odds 1:10 and p<0.05 the false positive rate is above 33% at any power; threshold 0.005 cuts this minimum to 5%.
limits: Proposed for new discoveries only, in fields with prior odds in a stated range. Bayes factor depends on the alternative assumed. Contested by other authors (not read).
agent_relevance: Gap 6 closed for Benjamin: the schema may cite BF about 3 (p=.05) vs BF about 20 (p=.005) as the evidence-strength mapping.

source: Button et al. (2013) Power failure: why small sample size undermines the reliability of neuroscience
finding: Nature page abstract opened. Median power across neuroscience is low; low power inflates effect sizes and lowers reproducibility.
numbers: Page abstract: median statistical power between about 8% and about 31% (depending on the subfield). The figure 21% from b09 is not on the page I could open; full text was paywalled.
limits: Full text not opened; use the 8-31% range, not 21%.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: replace 21% in claims with about 8-31%. Power failure is why small selection sets inflate gains (d02).

finding: Full text not reachable this session (paywalled; mirrors failed). Per-practice rates remain unchecked.
numbers: No new numbers. The 61% combined figure stays from memory.
agent_relevance: Do not cite per-practice false positive rates until the PDF is read.

source: Arce (2026) methods audit of forty-one self-improving LLM-agent papers, as cited by Hu and Tang
finding: Cited in the Hu and Tang bibliography: a 41-paper methods audit says most self-improving LLM-agent papers fail two or more evaluation traps.
numbers: Per title only: 'Most self-improving LLM-agent papers fail two or more evaluation traps: a methods audit of forty-one papers'. Not opened; cited link is an unusual alphaXiv URL.
agent_relevance: Context for gaps 1 and 9: the field's own audits find missing held-out controls.

source: Hu and Tang (2026) The Winner's Curse in LLM Self-Improvement Loops (candidate diversity)
finding: Candidates sampled from the same model are correlated and resemble each other more than the incumbent.
numbers: Correlation of candidate errors 0.44-0.60. Selection noise is shared by all candidates: after shrinkage the error of the reported gain still ranges -8.5 to +5.8 points within a setting.
limits: Prompt rewrites, not reasoning samples. Not a self-consistency study.
agent_relevance: Gap 10 partly: samples from one model act as partial, not independent, replicates. A shared bias cannot be averaged out. Direct vote-accuracy vs diversity measurement not found.

source: Hu and Tang (2026) The Winner's Curse in LLM Self-Improvement Loops (which gains survive)
finding: Larger selection sets help on TREC but not GSM8K, so which gains survive depends on task type. Big gains from weak starts stay big; marginal gains are within noise.
numbers: GEPA held-out gain on TREC did not grow with validation size (18.5, 20.4, 19.0 with 16, 64, 256 items). 14B proposer: TREC gains 26 to 33 points; Qwen3.5-4B from a one-sentence seed: 37-39 points TREC, 13-15 Banking77, at every n.
limits: Large gains came from a weak starting prompt.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: big gains from weak starts survive; gains of a few points sit inside selection noise. Mirrors the replication finding that large, simple effects replicate.
